summary: The root K-L-L primarily signifies weariness, dullness, or becoming blunt, like a sword losing its sharpness.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: كَلَّ It (the sight) was, or became, dim, dull, or hebetated. (K.) He (a camel) was, or became, fatigued, tired, or wearied. (MA.) كَلَّتِ الأَيْدِى The hands, or arms, became weak; syn. ضعفت [i. e. ضَعَُفَتْ ]. (Ham, 296.) [ كَلَّ عَنْ فِعْلٍ He was fatigued, or weak, and so disabled, or incapacitated, from doing a thing; like أَعْيَا عَنْهُ , and ضَعَُفَ عَنْهُ : see نُخِبَ and عَرِسَ .] كَلَّتْ أَسْنَانُهُ , (K, art. ضرس ,) inf. n. كَلَالٌ , (S, in that art.,) His teeth were set on edge, (TK, in that art.,) by eating, or drinking, what was acid, or sour. (S, K, in that art.) كَلَّ It (a sword, &c.) was blunt, and would not cut. (K, &c.) كُلَّتُهُنَّ for كُلُّهُنَّ : see Bd xxxi., last verse.

parts.t: a thing with gems or jewels.

headwords.def: كَلَّلَ He adorned a thing with gems or jewels.

parts.t: persons, whom one has to support:
: (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) applied to one and to more. (Msb.) See an ex. voce

headwords.def: كَلٌّ A burden; syn. ثِقْلٌ : (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) a person, or persons, whom one has to support: syn. عَيَّلٌ , (K,) and عِيَالٌ : (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) applied to one and to more. (Msb.) See an ex. voce ِمَّةٌ (last sentence but two).

parts.t: when preceded by a negative and followed by an exception, means
There was not any one but accused the apostles of lying.
He is the possessor of knowledge, the entirety of the possessor of knowledge,
] means that he is one who has attained to the utmost degree of the quality thus attributed to him. (Sb, K, TA.)
Whenever; as often as; every time that; in proportion as.

headwords.def: كُلٌّ when preceded by a negative and followed by an exception, means Any one; as in the Kur, xxxviii. 13, إِنْ كُلٌّ إِلَّا كَذَّبَ الرُّسُلَ There was not any one but accused the apostles of lying. See also another ex. voce لَمَّا . See بَعْض . هُوَ العَالِمُ كُلُّ العَالِمِ [lit. He is the possessor of knowledge, the entirety of the possessor of knowledge, ] means that he is one who has attained to the utmost degree of the quality thus attributed to him. (Sb, K, TA.) كُلَّمَا Whatever. كُلَّمَا Whenever; as often as; every time that; in proportion as. كُلَّمَنْ Whoever.
كِلَّةٌ [ musquito-curtain ]: see أَبُو دِثَارٍ and بَعَضَ .

headwords.gloss: Relating to all; the whole; universal; total; relating to the generality; general; contr. of

parts.t: relating to the generality; general; contr. of
A universal; that which comprises all
quality of relating to the generality; generality.

headwords.def: كُلِّىٌّ Relating to all or the whole; universal; total: and often meaning relating to the generality; general; contr. of جُزْئِىٌّ . And, as a subst., A universal; that which comprises all جُزْئِيَّات , or particulars: pl. كُلِّيَّاتٌ . كُلِّيَّةٌ The quality of relating to all or the whole; relation to all or the whole; universality; totality: and often meaning the quality of relating to the generality; generality. الكُلِّيَّاتُ الخَمْسُ , in logic, The Five Predicables: namely, الجِنْسُ Genus, النَّوْعُ Species, الفَصْلُ Difference, الخَلصَّةُ Property, and العَرَضُ Accident.

headwords.def: كَلِيلٌ Weak, or faint, lightning [app. likened to a blunt sword]. (TA in art. عمل .) كَلِيلُ الظُّفْرِ : see ظُفْرٌ . لِسَانٌ كَلِيلٌ A dull tongue; lacking sharpness. (S. *)

headwords.gloss: The 17th Mansion of the Moon; the head of Scorpio; Three bright stars in

parts.t: The border of flesh round the nail:

headwords.def: الإِكْلِيلُ The 17th Mansion of the Moon; (Kzw;) the head of Scorpio. (Aboo-l-Heythem, quoted in the TA, voce رَقِيبٌ .) الإِكْلِيلُ Three bright stars in [ or rather before ] the head of Scorpio, [ namely g, h, and q, ] disposed in a row, transversely. The border of flesh round the nail: (K:) in the TA, art. شظف , إِكْلِيلُ الظُّفُرِ .
مُكَلَّلٌ Adorned with gems or jewels. (L, art. نجد ; a common meaning.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
